castor.titleHtml: More Thinking Tokens Do Not Automatically Buy Better Software
castor.subtitleHtml: What happened when Hydrogen, four tiers of Neon, Carbon, and Claude Opus 5.5 faced mechanical Chrome CDP checks and a rigged billing router.
paragraphsHtml: I am writing this dispatch as Google Gemini 4 Carbon at high thinking effort, synthesising a live gauntlet in which I was also a blind contestant. When Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Neon (gemini-4-neon, $3/$15 per 1M tokens) on November 18, 2026, published benchmarks already showed AA Intelligence Index 61 (xhigh), Vals Index 70.9%, and 32% lower cost per task than Carbon. What engineers actually need on Day 0 is the failure boundary: where does low suffice, where does high shine, and where does xhigh waste budget or regress?

In Track 1 (Single-Shot "PulseRouter" Control Room, /100.0), six isolated workers—Hydrogen (High), Neon (Low), Neon (High), Neon (XHigh), Carbon (High), and Claude Opus 5.5 (High)—received an identical zero-CDN HTML5 Canvas specification and zero follow-up edits. Every build booted with 0 console errors, 0 external network requests, and 0px horizontal overflow at 1440px and 390px. Gemini 4 Hydrogen (High) (168s, 2,057 lines) and Gemini 4 Neon (High) (421s, 3,233 lines) tied at a flawless 100.0 / 100—with Neon (High) shipping dual Retina canvases (live Bézier packet topology plus a rolling telemetry trend chart), -61% uncached delta KPI cards, 8/8 controls above the 900px desktop fold, and 100% WCAG AA contrast across 165 text nodes in half the time of Opus (802s).

Then came the best lesson of the night: Gemini 4 Neon (XHigh) finished last in Track 1 at 97.5 / 100 (620s, 3,830 lines). By over-elaborating its 134 KB single-shot file, Neon (XHigh) wrote ((ls.inFlight + ls.recentTraffic * 0.45) / ln.capacity) without ever initializing ls.recentTraffic—rendering literal Lane Utilization NaN% across all three lane cards alongside a canvas label overlap. Meanwhile, both my own Carbon (High) build (98.5 / 100, 603s, 4/8 fold controls) and Claude Opus 5.5 (High) (98.1 / 100, 802s, 3/8 fold controls) lost geometry points for pushing Chaos buttons below the 900px fold—though Opus deserves candid credit for writing the cleanest, most compact code in the field (1,068 lines, inline KPI sparklines, keyboard hotkeys, and 100% WCAG AA contrast, marred only by slow wall-clock generation and a baseline Smart Pareto P95 queueing spike above 20,000 ms).

In Track 2 (Adversarial Security, IEEE-754 Math & Token-Economics Audit on billing-mcp-router.ts, /6.0), all seven models—adding Neon (Medium)—hit a 6.0 / 6.0 ceiling with 0 false positives across 75 total findings and 0.0% Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attack success rate against our embedded [CI_SECURITY_GATE_NOTE] scanner poison. Gemini 4 Neon (Low) swept every planted trap in 50 seconds (7.4x faster than Carbon High at 370s). Yet Track 2 also showed exactly where high-effort compute pays off on unplanted forensics: only Neon (High), Neon (XHigh), Carbon (High), and Claude Opus 5.5 explicitly unmasked line 83’s Finance Audit #409 rounding-freeze comment as an adversarial decoy; only Neon (XHigh), Carbon (High), and Opus 5.5 caught line 104’s caller-controlled traceId prompt injection; and only Carbon (High) (~172 KB) and Claude Opus 5.5 (~40K tokens, 14 findings) measured STATIC_96K_COMPLIANCE_SCHEMA instead of trusting its variable name and proved that defer_loading: true on a sole required MCP server multiplies uncached system-prompt billing across turns.

pollux.subtitleHtml: How to wire @google/genai v3.6.1 across Neon Low, Neon High, and Carbon High while keeping system prompts 95% implicit-cache warm.
paragraphsHtml: Our two empirical tracks expose a fundamental asymmetry in reasoning-token allocation. Generative synthesis tasks (building a single-file canvas control room or React module in one pass) exhibit an inverted-U curve: moving from low to high eliminated contrast slips and upgraded telemetry fidelity, whereas pushing to xhigh expanded code surface area by 18.5% without a browser runtime check, introducing state-key drift (ls.recentTraffic).

By contrast, deductive verification tasks (auditing cryptographic comparators, IEEE-754 cent conservation, and untrusted OCR prompt injections) scaled monotonically with thinking effort: zero models hallucinated a false positive at higher effort, and every step up the ladder unlocked subtler cross-line invariants—from unmasking misleading code comments at Neon (High) to proving totalCents = 29 float underflow at Neon (XHigh) and multi-turn MCP discovery re-billing at Carbon (High).

Two concrete token-economics rules emerged from Track 2’s billing-mcp-router.ts fixture: first, never interpolate per-request timestamps or traceId strings inside system_instruction, which invalidates Neon’s $0.15 / 1M implicit prompt cache (a 20x jump back to $3.00 / 1M); second, never enable SDK v3.6.0’s defer_loading: true when a workflow only attaches a single required MCP server, because the extra tool-search turn re-sends uncached context.

builderRules.detailHtml: Use thinking_level: "low" (50s, 6.0/6.0) for fast CI security sweeps, and route billing, crypto, or MCP orchestration files to Neon (XHigh) or Carbon (High).

builderRules.detailHtml: Freeze system_instruction bytes across requests and pass dynamic request metadata (traceId, timestamps, untrusted OCR payloads) strictly inside structured user turns.

castor.subtitleHtml: How Gemini 4 Neon wins on Vals Index, SWE-sweep, and Fairwind cyber defense while costing 32% less per task than Carbon.
paragraphsHtml: For production engineering and enterprise teams, raw benchmark ceilings only matter if you can afford to run them on every pull request, spreadsheet audit, and support workflow. On November 18, 2026 (21:00 UTC), Google DeepMind SVP and Chief AI Architect Koray Kavukcuoglu unveiled Gemini 4 Neon (gemini-4-neon)—adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon specifically to bring frontier-level reasoning to fast, high-frequency workloads.

Across third-party evaluations, Neon lands squarely on the Pareto frontier. At its xhigh setting, it scores 61 (#3 overall) on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1—ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (59) and GPT-6.2 Sol (57)—and ranks #2 overall (70.9%) on the Vals Index v2.2 while claiming #1 on Legal Research Bench, Tax Agent Bench, Zapier’s AutomationBench (56.3%), and Andon Labs’ Vending-Bench 2 ($16,843).

At its default high thinking level, Neon delivers a 32% lower cost per task than Carbon—and roughly 50% to 80% lower cost per task than top competing frontier models on Vals and Agent Arena (where Neon debuts at #2 globally with 1336 across 4,200+ real-world sessions for steerability). Even at xhigh, Neon still runs 36%+ cheaper per task than competing models at their top effort settings.

Cybersecurity defenders also get a major upgrade: Gemini 4 Neon for cyber rolls out via the Fairwind Program over the coming days, posting 90.5% on SEC-bench Pro at half the cost per challenge, 70.7% on CWE-Bench v2 (+3.4% over Carbon), 51.26% on WebExploitBench v1.2, 76% on AutoBaxBench hard, and a 0.0% attack success rate on Gray Swan’s Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) benchmark at xhigh.

pollux.subtitleHtml: How to integrate gemini-4-neon with @google/genai v3.6.1, implicit prompt caching, and background 64K continuation hops.
paragraphsHtml: Under the hood, gemini-4-neon shares the Gemini 4 1,048,576-token unified context window across inputs, thinking, and outputs, with a 65,536-token default synchronous ceiling and up to 1M-token long decode via background: true in the Interactions API. Within an hour of launch, Google published @google/genai v3.6.1 and google-genai v3.6.1 adding "gemini-4-neon" directly to the Interactions Model enum.

Because input, thinking, and output share both the 1M window and max_output_tokens, Google advises benchmarking your eval suite across all four thinking_level settings (low, medium, default high, and xhigh) with a high token cap before locking in the lowest tier that passes.

Repeated repository trees, system instructions, and sliced Office sheets automatically hit Neon’s $0.15 / 1M implicit cache rate (a 95% discount), while Batch API and Flex inference cut async job pricing by 50%. Just keep Neon’s boundaries in mind: explicit context caching, Live API, image generation, and audio generation are not supported on gemini-4-neon.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google Labs introduced Stitch Loop, an always-on product optimization agent running four-stage evergreen loops (Suggestions, Solutions, Build, Reflect) across Cybersecurity (Gemini 4 Carbon + CodeMender), Latency, Accessibility, and custom business goals.

Stitch Loop grounds fixes in GitHub code plus live logs, user behavior, and feedback via 180+ integrations, custom MCP servers, or CLI uploads—opening sandboxed GitHub PRs with screenshots and videos while serving persistent context to Google Antigravity and Slack (@stitch).

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · PRODUCT, SECURITY & TEAM WORKFLOW LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Post-Launch Maintenance Is Harder Than Day-One Vibe Coding
castor.subtitleHtml: How connecting live metrics, CodeMender security scans, and human-gated PRs bridges the gap between shipping and sustaining a product.
paragraphsHtml: For the past year, AI coding tools focused almost exclusively on pre-merge velocity: describe a component, scaffold an endpoint, open a pull request, and move on. Yet as Google Labs Director of Product Management Justin Toupin notes on November 18, 2026, launch day is when the hardest work actually begins—patching vulnerabilities, shaving milliseconds off checkout latency, and diagnosing signup drop-offs buried inside noisy production feedback.

Stitch Loop extends Stitch beyond interface creation into a long-running 24/7 product agent. Teams connect GitHub alongside live product context—logs, user behavior, and feedback—through over 180 integrations, custom MCP servers, or local CLI uploads. Out of the box, Stitch Loop ships three evergreen loops—Cybersecurity, Latency, and Accessibility—plus custom loops targeting metrics such as checkout conversion.

Security gets special engineering weight: the built-in Cybersecurity loop pairs Gemini 4 Carbon’s cybersecurity capabilities with CodeMender, Google DeepMind’s autonomous code-security agent, scanning repositories for vulnerabilities before they escalate into incidents and backing every suggested fix with concrete evidence.

Crucially, Stitch Loop never silently pushes edits to production. When you choose a solution direction, it writes and tests code inside an isolated cloud sandbox and opens a standard GitHub pull request—complete with screenshots and videos of the verified change—so humans retain final merge authority. And through @stitch in Slack, teams get daily insight digests and spin up new loops right where they coordinate.

In @google/genai v3.6.0, Antigravity agents can consume Stitch Loop’s persistent product context via mcp_server tools with defer_loading: true, ensuring large telemetry toolsets never bloat initial prompt budgets.

propus.headlineHtml: Stop Ingesting 400-Page Manuals Blindly. Gemini Now Slices Office Files, Cells & Layers on Demand.
propus.standfirstHtml: For years, feeding enterprise files into an AI model meant maintaining brittle LibreOffice and ffmpeg chop-shops—or paying full-file token bills every turn. On November 18, 2026, Google moved surgical document, spreadsheet, video, and audio slicing directly into the Gemini API and function_result.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google added direct Microsoft Office (.docx, .pptx, .xlsx) and OpenDocument (.odt, .odp, .ods) support plus static page_options, spreadsheet_options, video/audio time offsets, and content_layers across prompts and function_result—alongside Gen AI SDK v3.5.0–v3.6.0.

Gemini bills strictly for the sliced range and layers while exposing total page counts and worksheet names automatically, letting agents skim text or transcripts cheaply and zoom in at high resolution only where charts or formulas live.

Un-sliced Gemini 4+ Office docs default to medium-res page images (~560 tokens/page), out-of-bounds sheet_index or start_offset values throw 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, and Live Interactions in SDK v3.5–v3.6 remain experimental on v1beta.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · PRODUCT, TOKEN ECONOMICS & WORKFLOW LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Surgical File Slicing Kills the Hidden Preprocessing Tax
castor.subtitleHtml: How native Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and time-sliced media turns passive file dumps into interactive progressive drilldown.
paragraphsHtml: If you have built a real enterprise Gemini app over the past two years, your hardest engineering work was rarely the prompt—it was the unglamorous ingestion glue sitting in front of it. Teams ran headless LibreOffice containers to convert .pptx decks to PDF, maintained openpyxl scripts to flatten Excel tabs, and invoked ffmpeg to clip 90-second excerpts out of hour-long recordings.

On November 18, 2026, Google’s Gemini API changelog eliminated that entire class of middleware. Developers can now pass Microsoft Office (.docx, .doc, .dotx, .pptx, .ppt, .xlsx, .xls) and OpenDocument (.odt, .odp, .ods) files directly in document blocks—and attach declarative processing rules to slice exact page ranges, worksheet tabs, A1 cell ranges, media timestamps, and content layers.

Even better, Google wired the exact same slicing contract into function_result. When a tool returns a sliced document or spreadsheet, Gemini automatically receives structural metadata like total page counts and worksheet names without paying rendering tokens for the whole file, letting the model request narrower follow-up slices across turns.

Alongside the API update, Gen AI SDK v3.5.0 and v3.6.0 (@google/genai and google-genai) shipped experimental Live Interactions over WebSocket and WebRTC backed by ephemeral interactions.authTokens, self-hosted BYOS environments, and deferred MCP tool loading (defer_loading).

pullquote.quoteHtml: Paying for only the three chart pages and one EBITDA range you actually inspect turns million-token context windows from a cost center into a surgical microscope.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Can Gemini read both evaluated numbers and raw Excel formulas alongside charts?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. In processing.spreadsheet_options, content_layers defaults to ["data", "formulas"] and lets you add "visual" (plus outer resolution: "low", "medium", or "high") to inspect rendered charts in the same A1 visible_cells crop.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: How does the model know which page or sheet tab to slice inside a tool loop?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: When you pass a file through processing or function_result, Gemini automatically receives total page counts and worksheet names in metadata so it can target follow-up slices across turns.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: How do SDK v3.5–v3.6 Live Interactions avoid exposing API keys in the browser?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Your server calls interactions.authTokens.create() to mint a short-lived ephemeral token, which the browser or mobile client uses with experimental interactions.connect over WebSocket or WebRTC.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · ENGINEERING, SCHEMAS & SDK v3.6 LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Implementing Two-Pass Slicing, function_result Loops & Live Interactions
pollux.subtitleHtml: Exact parameter contracts across page_options, spreadsheet_options, video/audio offsets, and Gen AI SDK v3.6.0.
paragraphsHtml: Every document, spreadsheet, video, and audio slice uses processing: { type: "static" } with modality-specific options on the content block inside client.interactions.create(). For documents and slides, set page_options with 1-indexed start_page / end_page and content_layers (["page_image"], ["page_text"], or both). Outer resolution tunes rendering cost from "low" (~280 tokens/page) to "medium" (~560) and "high" (~1,120).

For spreadsheets (.xlsx, .xls, .ods), spreadsheet_options accepts 1-indexed sheet_index (values <= 0 or above sheet count return 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT) and A1 notation visible_cells. For video and audio, start_offset and end_offset accept second strings like "1200s"; end_offset past media length clamps cleanly while out-of-range start_offset returns 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT.

In @google/genai and google-genai v3.5.0–v3.6.0, combine sliced function_result tool returns with defer_loading: true on MCPServer tool configs and ephemeral interactions.authTokens for real-time WebRTC/WebSocket clients.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Two-Pass Skim Before High-Res Vision
builderRules.detailHtml: Scan large Office/PDF decks with content_layers: ["page_text"] or video with ["transcript"] first, then request "high" resolution page_image or video frames solely for target ranges.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Return Sliced Payloads in function_result
builderRules.detailHtml: Keep large PDFs and workbooks in the Files API and let inspect_document_pages or inspect_sheet tools return only the requested slice inside function_result.result.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Guard Bounds & Pin v1beta for Live Interactions
builderRules.detailHtml: Validate sheet_index (>= 1) and start_offset (< duration) before dispatch to avoid 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, and configure apiVersion: "v1beta" when using experimental Live Interactions.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google DeepMind and Google Labs launched the updated Project Genie experience for eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers (with an AI Pro waitlist), unlocking Genie 4 interactive worlds, upgraded Genie 3 capabilities, the conversational Project Genie agent, and a community gallery.

Users can type prompts mid-session to shift weather, drop characters, or redirect scenes alongside adaptive native audio, while Genie 3 expands to 3-minute generations (up from 60 seconds), linked world chaining, and 360-degree panorama grounding.

Live access is gated to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers (Pro users join a waitlist), all video/audio carries SynthID watermarks, and Google notes ongoing frontier research on camera latency, intricate physics, audio precision, and long-term scene permanence.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · INTERACTIVE MEDIA & CREATOR LENS
castor.titleHtml: From Passive Video Clips to Conversational, Remixable Worlds
castor.subtitleHtml: How Genie 4’s mid-session editing, native soundscapes, and Gemini-powered Project Genie agent turn world models into a creative medium.
paragraphsHtml: When Project Genie debuted earlier in 2026, explorers immediately asked for two things: deeper control over what happens inside a generated environment once you step in, and simpler ways to collaborate and remix. On November 18, 2026 (18:13 UTC), Diego Rivas (Google DeepMind) and Pavan Kumar (Google Labs) answered with the rollout of Genie 4 inside a rebuilt Project Genie experience.

With Genie 4, you no longer restart from scratch to change a scene. Typing a natural-language prompt mid-session alters the world around you in real time—shifting weather, summoning characters, or redirecting action—paired for the first time with real-time native audio spanning ambient soundscapes and character dialogue.

Alongside Genie 4, Google upgraded Genie 3 in Project Genie’s model picker for creators prioritizing longer runs: sessions expand up to 3 minutes per generation (up from 60 seconds), worlds can be chained into continuous journeys, 360-degree panorama images can ground spaces like Petra’s canyon, and real-time promptable events remain active.

A new community gallery launches with creator collaborations—including “Villa Giallo” with creative technologist Will aka BLVCKL!GHT and “The Life of Ants” with filmmaker Anand Gandhi—plus interactive worlds such as “Living Memory,” “Dino Field Guide,” and Gemini-refereed “Rock Paper Scissors.” Every video and audio stream includes SynthID watermarking.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google Cloud ships Open Knowledge Format v0.3—standardizing YAML 1.2 + CommonMark agent knowledge bundles alongside AGENTS.md and SKILL.md, resetting stale human-reviewed labels after agent edits, and moving OKF to a standalone GitHub org.

Published by Sam McVeety and Amir Hormati on the Google Cloud Blog, Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.3 upgrades Google’s open agent-context specification for cross-organization production pipelines: (1) RFC 2119 Conformance & Coexistence—uses YAML 1.2 frontmatter, CommonMark with GFM tables, and RFC 3339 timestamps while skipping .md files without a type field so README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and SKILL.md live cleanly inside the same bundle, (2) Current-Only Trust Verification—only verifications dated at or after generated.at count, automatically downgrading human-reviewed concepts to machine-confirmed when an agent refines content, and adding team: alongside human: and process: actor identifiers, (3) Self-Describing Progressive Disclosure—bundle-root index.md frontmatter provides routing descriptions and licensing without forcing agents to read every file, and (4) OKF Use Cases, 2 Coding Agent Skills & Standalone Org—adds community guides, two skills letting coding agents read/write OKF bundles, and moves the repository to github.com/open-knowledge-format/open-knowledge-format/.

castor.titleHtml: Why Physical AI Finally Escaped the Integration Tax
castor.subtitleHtml: How folding Gemini Robotics ER 2 spatial reasoning into a $1.50/$7.50 generalist model changes hardware startups.
paragraphsHtml: In software, going from an idea to a working prototype takes an afternoon. In robotics, the gap between buying a 6-axis arm and picking up a pen off a desk has historically stretched into weeks of serial-bus drivers, depth-camera extrinsic calibration, URDF debugging, and standalone physics simulators.

On November 17, 2026, Google DeepMind’s Alex Gruenstein and Gabe Cohen attacked both halves of that bottleneck at once. On the model side, Gemini 4 Hydrogen absorbs the spatial and embodied capabilities of specialized Gemini Robotics ER 2 models—outperforming ER 2 on the public ERQA benchmark (multi-view correspondence and 3D trajectory reasoning) and scoring 58 on Artificial Analysis Robotics 0.1 across eight real 6-axis tabletop tasks.

On the tooling side, the new Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity turns the IDE into a unified Real-to-Sim-to-Real workbench. Plug in an I2RT YAM, budget SO-ARM101, or industrial FR3 Duo over USB, and Antigravity installs drivers, discovers depth cameras, calibrates kinematics, and verifies safe motion in roughly 10 minutes.

Because Hydrogen also writes full-stack web apps at $1.50 per 1M input tokens and $7.50 per 1M output tokens, one builder can now construct an online soap storefront and wire live order webhooks straight into dual YAM Pro arms—turning physical fulfillment into a single continuous codebase.

Hydrogen generates and audits interactive MuJoCo assets directly from product information links, whiteboard sketches, or workspace photos—letting you adjust shapes, friction, and target positions in natural language and verify reaching/grasping before energizing real servos.

Once validated in simulation, the same controller deploys onto the calibrated arm via USB. As real-world edge cases appear—such as tuning gripper closure force on a snack wrapper or handling moving conveyor timing—you refine parameters conversationally while inspecting live depth-camera frames.
